chunks: Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said to a man: 'You have been made to be a physician yourself, and the illness has been clarified to you, and you have been made to recognize the sign of health, and you have been indicated upon the cure, therefore look how you are standing (burdened) upon yourself'.
ai.seo_question: What is the metaphor of the physician in Shia hadith regarding self-accountability?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) employs the medical metaphor of *al-tibb al-nafs* (self-healing) to emphasize individual accountability (*mas'uliyya*) in spiritual practice. He asserts that since the pathology of the soul, the indicators of its health, and the prescribed remedies have been explicitly revealed, the believer must actively monitor his own spiritual state. This reflects the Shia emphasis on the intellect (*'aql*) as the internal guide that complements prophetic revelation in diagnosing and curing the soul's ailments.

en.hubeali: ‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said to a man: ‘You have been made to be a physician yourself, and the illnesses have been clarified to you, and you have recognises the signs of good health, and you have been indicated upon the medication, therefore look how you are standing (burden) upon yourself’.
en.sarwar: 6. It is narrated from him (narrator of the Hadith above) in a marfu’ manner from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.)

who has said the following to a man: “You have been made the physician for your own self. Medicine is prescribed for you; signs of good health are shown to you, and the direction for medicine is given to you. It is all up to you how you treat yourself.”
